title: Psalm Titles
lead: Many psalms open with a heading naming an author, a tune, an instrument or an occasion. Thirteen tie a psalm to a moment in David's life, most of them during his years as a fugitive from Saul.

sections.h: Headings that name a moment in David's life
sections.b: Thirteen psalm titles name an event: Psalm 3 (fleeing Absalom), Psalm 7 (Cush the Benjaminite), Psalm 18 (rescue from Saul and all enemies), Psalm 34 (feigning madness before Abimelech), Psalm 51 (Nathan after Bathsheba), Psalm 52 (Doeg's report), Psalm 54 (the Ziphites), Psalm 56 (seized in Gath), Psalm 57 (in the cave), Psalm 59 (Saul's men watching the house), Psalm 60 (wars with Aram and Edom), Psalm 63 (in the wilderness of Judah) and Psalm 142 (in the cave). In Hebrew Bibles the title is counted as verse 1, so verse numbers often run one higher than in English; this site cites a title as verse 0. Most scholars think the titles were added by later editors, as Brevard Childs argued, reading David's life to find settings for the prayers. Traditional readers take them as original or reliable. Either way, they are among the oldest interpretations of Samuel.
